Recurrent-Event PROC PHREG Parity (SAS Recurrent-Admission Baseline)

Source: R/sas_phreg_parity.R
cgd_recurrent_data.Rd

The SAS recurrent-admission baseline: a `PROC PHREG` counterpart to the package's recurrent-event Cox fits. The SAS side is the benchmark program `inst/sas/benchmark_recurrent_phreg.sas` (plain `PROC PHREG`, no macro); the R side here fits the same models from [recurrent_cox()], parses a SAS listing back into the same shape, and compares the two.

Usage

cgd_recurrent_data()

recurrent_phreg_quantities(
  data,
  predictors = c("treat", "sex", "age"),
  id = "id",
  start = "tstart",
  stop = "tstop",
  status = "status",
  models = c("ag", "pwp_gap"),
  max_events = 3L,
  conf_level = 0.95
)

parse_recurrent_phreg_lst(lines)

compare_recurrent_phreg(r, sas, atol = 6e-06, rtol = 0)

# S3 method for class 'recurrent_phreg_comparison'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame of counting-process intervals.

predictors

Covariates: a character vector of column names, or a one-sided formula such as `~ treat + sex + age`. Default `c("treat", "sex", "age")`, the benchmark model.

id, start, stop, status

Column names (strings) of the subject identifier, the interval start and stop, and the event indicator (0/1 or logical).

models

Which fits to run: any subset of `"ag"` and `"pwp_gap"`.

max_events

For the `"pwp_gap"` fit, event numbers above `max_events` are pooled into one stratum (default `3`, the strata of the SAS program). Passed to [recurrent_cox()].

conf_level

Confidence level of the hazard ratios (default `0.95`).

lines

Character vector of listing lines (from a `.lst` file, as read by [readLines()]), or a single path to one.

r, sas

Quantity tables as returned by [recurrent_phreg_quantities()] and [parse_recurrent_phreg_lst()].

atol, rtol

Absolute and relative tolerances for the estimates and standard errors (SAS prints those to 5 decimals, so the absolute tolerance alone covers the rounding; `rtol` defaults to 0 so a relative allowance cannot hide a real discrepancy). P-values use an absolute tolerance of 1e-4 and hazard ratios an absolute 6e-4, because SAS prints p-values to 4 decimals and hazard ratios to 3 (half a unit in the last place is 5e-5 and 5e-4 respectively).

x

A `recurrent_phreg_comparison` returned by [compare_recurrent_phreg()].

...

Unused; present for consistency with [print()].

Value

[cgd_recurrent_data()]: a tibble with `id`, `tstart`, `tstop`, `status`, `treat` (1 = rIFN-g), `sex` (1 = female), `age` and `enum`. [recurrent_phreg_quantities()]: a tibble with `model`, `term`, `estimate` (log hazard ratio), `std_error` (robust sandwich), `std_error_model` (model-based, from the fit's naive covariance), `hazard_ratio`, `p_value` (robust Wald) and `p_value_model` (model-based Wald). [parse_recurrent_phreg_lst()]: a tibble with `model`, `se_type` (`"robust"` or `"model"`), `term`, `estimate`, `std_error`, `std_error_ratio` (`NA` for model-based rows), `statistic` (Wald chi-square), `p_value` and `hazard_ratio`. [compare_recurrent_phreg()]: a list of class `recurrent_phreg_comparison` with `table` (one row per compared quantity, with `r_value`, `sas_value`, `abs_diff` and `matched`) and `matched` (single `TRUE`/`FALSE`).

Benchmark data and model

Both sides fit `survival::cgd`, the chronic granulomatous disease trial (203 counting-process intervals for 128 patients, 76 recurrent infections), as returned by [cgd_recurrent_data()]: `treat` recoded to 1 = rIFN-g, 0 = placebo, `sex` to 1 = female, 0 = male, `age` in years. The model on both sides is `(tstart, tstop) * status(0) = treat sex age`, with `TIES=EFRON` in SAS (matching [recurrent_cox()], which fits with Efron ties – not the SAS default Breslow, which moves the coefficients in the 4th-5th decimal) and `COVS(AGGREGATE)` with `ID id` in SAS (the Lin-Wei robust sandwich standard errors that [recurrent_cox()] reports). Two fits are compared: `"ag"` (Andersen-Gill, total time, one baseline hazard) and `"pwp_gap"` (Prentice-Williams-Peterson gap time, baseline hazard per event number, event numbers pooled at `max_events = 3` – strata 1, 2 and 3-or-later, holding 44, 17 and 15 events – on gap times that restart at the previous infection). No other `recurrent_cox()` model has a SAS counterpart in this benchmark.

Status

The program was run once on SAS 9.4 (TS1M8, Windows) on 12 Nov 2026; the listing is stored as `inst/sas/list/benchmark_recurrent_phreg.lst` and the log as `inst/sas/logs/benchmark_recurrent_phreg.log` (no errors or warnings). The R quantities agree with that listing at the per-quantity tolerances of [compare_recurrent_phreg()] (Tier-1 test in `tests/testthat/test-round2-0911-sas.R`), so [sas_parity_boundary()] lists this as `"parity"`. The claim covers the two fits and the `COVS(AGGREGATE)` / `COVM` standard errors on `survival::cgd` with Efron ties only. The stored log echoes the program's pre-run "DRAFT – never been run" header comment, because the `.sas` file was edited after the run; the log's SAS header (version, licence, date) and the absence of any `ERROR:` or `WARNING:` line are what record that the run happened.

How to run it (on a machine with SAS 9.4)

Export the data from R with `write_sas_data(cgd_recurrent_data(), "cgdrec.xpt")`, put `cgdrec.xpt` beside `inst/sas/benchmark_recurrent_phreg.sas`, and run the program with `run_sas_script(sas_macro_path("benchmark_recurrent_phreg.sas"))` (or in SAS directly – the program header gives the batch command). Store the listing and log as `inst/sas/list/benchmark_recurrent_phreg.lst` and `inst/sas/logs/benchmark_recurrent_phreg.log`. Then, in R, `parse_recurrent_phreg_lst()` the stored listing and `compare_recurrent_phreg()` it against `recurrent_phreg_quantities(cgd_recurrent_data())`; a Tier-1 test in `tests/testthat/test-round2-0911-sas.R` does exactly that once the listing exists.

What the listing must contain

Each `PROC PHREG` run prints two "Analysis of Maximum Likelihood Estimates" tables – one "with Model-Based Variance Estimate" (from `COVM`) and one "with Sandwich Variance Estimate" (from `COVS(AGGREGATE)`, with an extra StdErr Ratio column). The parser keys each table to its fit by the program's title lines (`"Recurrent PHREG – Andersen-Gill ..."` / `"Recurrent PHREG – PWP gap time ..."`), and to its standard-error type by the table subtitle, falling back to the number of columns when a subtitle is absent. A p-value SAS prints as `<.0001` parses to `NA` and matches when the R p-value is below 1e-4, as in [compare_km_lifetest()].

See also

[sas_parity_boundary()], [recurrent_cox()], [compare_km_lifetest()], [sas_macro_path()], [run_sas_script()], [write_sas_data()]

Examples

cgd <- cgd_recurrent_data()
nrow(cgd)
#> [1] 203
recurrent_phreg_quantities(cgd)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 8
#>   model   term  estimate std_error std_error_model hazard_ratio  p_value
#>   <chr>   <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>           <dbl>        <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 ag      treat  -1.12      0.310           0.261         0.327 0.000309
#> 2 ag      sex    -0.0828    0.366           0.331         0.921 0.821   
#> 3 ag      age    -0.0300    0.0141          0.0133        0.970 0.0339  
#> 4 pwp_gap treat  -0.931     0.280           0.278         0.394 0.000870
#> 5 pwp_gap sex    -0.214     0.321           0.338         0.808 0.506   
#> 6 pwp_gap age    -0.0227    0.0109          0.0136        0.978 0.0370
